Record Class ItemMatch

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
com.trevlar.menukit.api.element.ItemMatch
Record Components:
stack - the rule's stack: the item, and for EXACT and CONTAINS its count and components
match - how a stack is compared with it
ignored - component types left out of the comparison (none by default)
countIgnored - whether EXACT leaves the count out (false by default)
public record ItemMatch(net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack stack, ItemMatch.Match match, Set<net.minecraft.core.component.DataComponentType<?>> ignored, boolean countIgnored) extends Record
An item rule: a stack and how another stack has to match it. What an ItemPicker slot holds, and the one comparison every mod uses, so none writes its own. 
// A rule the player set with an item picker, tested against a stack in play.
if (rule.matches(stack)) lock(slot);

// A plain stack and the mode the setting declares.
ItemMatch.matches(config.target, ItemMatch.Match.CONTAINS, stack);

The three modes

  • ItemMatch.Match.ITEM: the kind of item only. Count and components are ignored: any diamond sword is a diamond sword.
  • ItemMatch.Match.EXACT: vanilla's own stack equality (ItemStack.matches(ItemStack, ItemStack)): the same item, the same count, and exactly the same components. A rule with no components set is a plain item, so an enchanted or renamed one does not match it. The count matters for an item that stacks; one that does not is always one.
  • ItemMatch.Match.CONTAINS: the same item, and at least the components the rule sets; others may be there too, and the count is ignored. A rule with no components set matches any variant of the item. A component the rule removes (!food in /give syntax) must be absent.
Whether an empty rule means "plain" or "any" is the mode's answer, never a guess: EXACT says plain, CONTAINS says any.

Ignoring components, and the count

A rule can leave chosen component types out of the comparison, in EXACT and CONTAINS alike: neither side's value for them is looked at. A lock on "this exact sword" that should hold after the sword takes damage: 
ItemMatch lock = new ItemMatch(sword, ItemMatch.Match.EXACT)
        .ignoring(DataComponents.DAMAGE)   // still this sword once it is worn
        .ignoringCount();                  // and a stack of 3 is still "this item"
ignoringCount() drops the count from EXACT (the count is not a component, so it has its own call; CONTAINS and ITEM never compare it). Both are saved with the rule by CODEC, and a rule saved without them loads ignoring nothing, as before.

CONTAINS compares as vanilla's item predicates do

Each component the rule sets is compared the way an item predicate in a command or a datapack compares it (/clear @s diamond_sword[damage=0], and the partial ~ form where vanilla has one):
  • enchantments and stored_enchantments: the stack has at least the rule's enchantments, each at the rule's level (vanilla's EnchantmentsPredicate); it may have more.
  • custom_data: the rule's tag is contained in the stack's (vanilla's NBT predicate, CustomData.matchedBy(CompoundTag)).
  • Any other component: equal, as DataComponentExactPredicate compares it.

An empty rule (ItemStack.EMPTY, or air) matches nothing, and an empty stack matches no rule: an empty picker slot is not a rule.

Common code: it reads only the stacks, so a mod's server side can use it too. The record copies its stack; treat stack() as read-only. Two rules are equal when their modes are, their stacks match exactly (ItemStack.matches(ItemStack, ItemStack)), and they ignore the same.

  • Field Details

    • CODEC

      public static final com.mojang.serialization.Codec<ItemMatch> CODEC
      Saves a rule as {stack: <vanilla's stack>, match: "exact"}, plus ignoring: ["minecraft:damage"] and ignore_count: true when the rule has them (left out when it does not, so a rule saved before they existed loads as it was). The stack goes through vanilla's ItemStack.OPTIONAL_CODEC, so encode it with the world's registry ops (enchantments are registry entries), as vanilla saves a stack.

      public boolean equals(Object o)
      Indicates whether some other object is "equal to" this one. The objects are equal if the other object is of the same class and if all the record components are equal.
